subject: region.move_to_playhead against a live project, with one and with two regions selected
question: Does a selection carrying two regions make the operation report on one while moving both?

reverify.command: Park the playhead away from the regions (logic_transport.goto_position bar 5). Establish a known selection by clicking 편집 > 선택 > 전체 선택 해제 and then writing AXSelected=true once per region wanted. Call logic_edit.move_to_playhead through the built binary and read the envelope, then re-read every region's AXHelp for its start bar. Run the same thing again with exactly one region selected — that arm is the control and it decides whether the run says anything.
reverify.expected: unknown; on this host both arms reported no position change, which is what makes the run inconclusive rather than a result
reverify.cost: ~3 min, a project with two regions

method: Ran the case and its control in the same session against the same project, because the case alone cannot be read: an operation that does nothing produces the same envelope whether or not the blind spot exists. The control is the same call with a single region selected, which is the configuration the operation is written for.

observations.what: the case — two regions selected, playhead at bar 5
the control — exactly one region selected, same playhead
the harness I looked at, and the one I did not
observations.its_own_words: every call in this run is a read
observations.correction: there are four live_575_* harnesses; live_575_move_to_playhead_reachable.py DOES drive the operation and checks State A against the same region it started with. Reporting the first file's silence as absence was wrong.

observations.what: the code reading that prompted the run
observations.returns: the first region found with AXSelected true

conclusion: The run is inconclusive and the control is why. With the playhead at bar 5, `move_to_playhead` reported `no position change` and left every region at bar 1 — with two regions selected AND with one. An operation that moves nothing produces the same envelope in both arms, so nothing here supports or refutes the question that was asked. One claim made from this run has been WITHDRAWN: that nothing drives the operation. That came from looking at one of four similarly named harnesses; another of them exists to drive it. What the run does establish is narrower and still worth having: on this host, in this project, the operation did not move a region in either configuration, and it said so honestly rather than reporting a success. Separately, and by reading rather than measurement, the operation's pre/post readback is `selectedRegionInfo`, which answers with the first selected region while Logic's command acts on the whole selection — the same blind spot that `region.select_last` closed by reading the selection as a set. That remains a code reading, not a demonstrated defect.
limits: SUPERSEDED by 2026-09-05-move-to-playhead-works-and-what-hid-it: the operation works. This run's failure was session state the run did not know about — the Mixer was open, and while it holds the Edit menu the path this operation drives is not present. Kept because a run that was wrong for a reason worth knowing is evidence about the method.
The reason the operation moved nothing was not established. Focus, which editor is active, and whether the arrange area accepts the menu command in this state were all unexamined.
One project, one host, one session. No attempt was made on a second project or after restarting Logic.
The blind-spot question is UNANSWERED by this run. Do not cite it as evidence that the defect exists or that it does not.

The playhead move that set up the run reported State B `readback_unavailable` itself, with subdivision and tick unobserved, so `playhead_bar: 5` is the operation's own reading rather than an independent one.

The obvious next step was not taken here: `live_575_move_to_playhead_reachable.py` establishes the preconditions this operation needs and drives it, and running that is how to settle what hand-driving could not.
